leanWhy: The piece is largely a straight recap with extended direct quotes of Trump and the reporter's brief reply, with no editorializing. The headline and lead emphasize the finger-wagging and the "rude" remark, which is a slight tilt that makes Trump look bad, but the article also includes Trump's praise of Miller and his closing remarks without comment.

signals.quote: wagging his finger at her, calling her "really a rude person" and telling her she belonged in the "back row."
signals.why: Leading with the confrontation's most vivid details gives the exchange the prominence of a story in itself.

signals.quote: Who are you with. Who are you with?
signals.why: The reporter's original question or topic is not identified, so readers can't see what prompted the exchange.

title: Merchant Crew Ignores UN’s Advice, Thwarts Pirate Attack

title: Too many House Republicans are missing work, Mike Johnson says

The headline, the summary's "still getting paid" line and the lead's "skipped work" framing stress Republican absences and pay, which is a mild tilt against the GOP.

leanWhy: This is a thesis-driven opinion piece with an alarmist headline. It defends the Electoral College, attributes the left's motives to a power grab, and sets Buttigieg's quote against unflattering comparisons to other countries. The excerpt gives no opposing voices.

signals.quote: A national popular vote would destroy the United States
signals.why: The headline is an absolutist, alarmist claim that states the thesis as fact.

signals.quote: it has everything to do with grabbing power

signals.quote: the electoral process favored by Algeria, the Dominican Republic, and Turkey

signals.quote: everyone understands why left-wingers want direct popular presidential elections
